heading: Do better tools show polysemantic neurons mostly detect one feature or related offshoots?
definition: canonical polysemantic neurons turn out, with better tools, to detect one shared feature (e.g. pose) or related offshoots of one job, so truly unrelated mixtures are rare.
summary: Independent vision studies, and one polysemous-word study in language models, find some mixed-looking neurons that resolve to one shared feature or related offshoots, but the vision tools also split other hand-picked neurons into distinct features. The only independent random-sample estimate, on one ResNet-18 layer under a lenient criterion, finds 31% of 128 units still polysemantic, so the claim that unrelated mixtures are rare is contested, though no independent language-model study challenges it.

suggested_status.by_scale: Toy: no V6 study. Vision CNNs (ResNet-18/50, AlexNet, InceptionV1/V3; counts versions.V6.studies_by_size 'not stated' = 8): the 'rare' part fails on a random ResNet-18 sample (arXiv:2006.14032#r1: one model, one layer, lenient criterion), so C for the 'rare' part only. Hand-picked neurons that the finer tool splits into distinct features (arXiv:2404.06453, arXiv:2206.01627, arXiv:2304.09707, none marked SAME GROUP in the studies index) show that such neurons exist but give no rate. The narrower claim, that some single neurons resolve to one shared feature or to related offshoots, rests on three studies that the studies index does not mark SAME GROUP, which puts that part near R2. No pack header carries a SHARES AUTHORS flag, so this rests on the studies index (and, for arXiv:2006.14032, its author list), not on headers. They are arXiv:2404.06453#r24 (#271), arXiv:2006.14032#r2 (28 of the 88 meaningful units, where the authors read the shared percept by manual inspection) and arXiv:2304.09707#r3 (neuron 1, partial). arXiv:2406.03662's n/376 no longer counts here, because the check reads its V6 verdict as none. <1B ('<1B' = 2) and 1-10B ('1-10B' = 3): mixed, with no independent challenge to 'rare'. arXiv:2305.01610 challenges (Pythia 70M, 1B). The studies index marks it SAME GROUP and its author list shares authors with an original, so its challenges are not an independent failed test, and its supports (probe-selected is_passive_verb / is_title neurons) count as the original group's extension (R1 evidence), not as independent. arXiv:2610.24521 limits (Gemma 3 4B). Its authors have no name match with an original, but the critic notes Anthropic authors, an affiliation-only case for Iris to rule on. Independent support covers only polysemous words (arXiv:2604.00443), plus a GPT-2 XL anecdote. 10-100B ('10-100B' = 1): R0, with polysemous-word support only (arXiv:2604.00443#r01 spans 110M–70B). >100B: no key in versions.V6.studies_by_size. Claude 3 Sonnet (size not stated) challenges the version (arXiv:2605.29358#r1), but the studies index marks that study SAME GROUP, so the challenge is not independent.
suggested_status.reason: counts versions.V6.verdicts: supports in 7 studies, limits_scope in 3, challenges in 6 studies (7 verdicts). These keys were built before the check corrections, and the counts have not been rebuilt, so they still carry the old labels. The supports figure includes arXiv:2406.03662's verdict on mixed3b/n/376, which the check reads as none: the text lists n/376 among more monosemantic neurons, so it does not test V6. That study's only V6 verdict is limits_scope (n/44, n/359). Likewise, versions.V6.rows_by_state counts arXiv:2006.14032#r1 as observed, while its verdict fix and the check give its V6 state as absent. These keys need re-quoting once the fixes reach the records and the counts are rebuilt. versions.V6.studies_supports_only = 1, which is lw:JA5Eyf2cqyL3HbKxS, an anecdote with no method. C applies to the 'rare' part only. Its independent basis is a peer-reviewed random-sample estimate: 31% of 128 ResNet-18 units are still polysemantic after compositional explanation (arXiv:2006.14032#r1). That is one model and one layer, under a lenient criterion ('firing for at least some unrelated concepts'). The same ResNet-18 study's support (28 of the 88 meaningful units, arXiv:2006.14032#r2) rests on the authors reading one perceptual feature by manual inspection, not on the explanation search. The check keeps that supports label but corrects its condition: atomic labels do not make these units look mixed. Three studies that the studies index does not mark SAME GROUP have hand-picked vision neurons that the finer tool splits into distinct features (arXiv:2404.06453, arXiv:2206.01627, arXiv:2304.09707). They show that such neurons exist but give no rate. Inspection of random Claude 3 Sonnet neurons also contradicts 'rare' (arXiv:2605.29358#r1). But the studies index marks that study SAME GROUP and its author list shares authors with an original, so it is not an independent failed test. Neither are the Pythia n-gram neurons of arXiv:2305.01610 (r1, r4). In language models no independent study challenges 'rare'. The independent support there is the GPT-2 XL anecdote and the polysemous-word study below. Per the completeness critic, neither side of the conflict between lw:JA5Eyf2cqyL3HbKxS and arXiv:2605.29358 is on the reading list. Most studies that find a shared feature or related offshoots for some neurons find distinct features for others with the same tool (arXiv:2404.06453, arXiv:2304.09707, arXiv:2305.01610). The studies index marks arXiv:2305.01610 SAME GROUP and its author list shares authors with an original, so its V6 support counts as R1. No pack header carries a SHARES AUTHORS mark. counts versions.V6.tested_sharing_an_author_with_an_original = 2 is this study plus arXiv:2605.29358, the two V6 studies that the index marks SAME GROUP; the original carries no mark. The canonical neuron 4e:55 is never re-analysed: versions.V6.original_sources_linked lists only the Zoom In essay, which reads it as having no shared feature (DOI:10.23915/distill.00024.001#R2). In language models the independent support covers only word form on polysemous words (arXiv:2604.00443). That study's lexical adjustment is a conservative lower bound limited to the top-50 form detectors per word, and it gives no rate of unrelated mixtures.
suggested_status.open_questions: Would SAEs or attribution clustering on InceptionV1 4e:55 and other Zoom In examples show a pose or other shared feature? After per-neuron SAE, transcoder or attribution analysis, what share of randomly sampled neurons still shows unrelated mixtures, in InceptionV1 and in language models? Does the 31% from arXiv:2006.14032 hold when such tools replace compositional formulas, in other models and layers, and under a stricter criterion than 'firing for at least some unrelated concepts'? Would a method other than manual inspection confirm the shared perceptual feature in its 28 units (arXiv:2006.14032#r2)? Would an independent group reproduce the related-offshoot readings of probe-selected Pythia neurons (arXiv:2305.01610)? Would a group other than the original's find unrelated mixtures common among random language-model neurons? Both language-model challenges to 'rare' are same-group (arXiv:2605.29358#r1, arXiv:2305.01610#r1, #r4). Does arXiv:2610.24521, with Anthropic authors but no name match with an original, count as independent? Iris rules on this affiliation-only case. Can relatedness be scored by an agreed criterion, given that CLIP and attribution clustering disagree (arXiv:2404.06453#r24)? A random-sample result showing that most mixtures resolve to one feature would move the 'rare' part off C.

source.title: Zoom In: An Introduction to Circuits
source.authors: Chris Olah; Nick Cammarata; Ludwig Schubert; Gabriel Goh; Michael Petrov; Shan Carter

original_result.setup: Olah et al. used feature visualization on InceptionV1 neuron 4e:55 to check whether its cat and car inputs share a common feature.
original_result.result: They found no shared feature: the neuron looks for eyes and whiskers of a cat, furry legs, and shiny fronts of cars. This covers one hand-picked neuron and gives no rate across neurons.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: 28 of 88 meaningful units joined seemingly unrelated concepts sharing one perceptual feature.
Clustering activations split one neuron's responses into two related directions, both parts of one feature.
Beyond their target feature, title and passive-verb neurons fired on related features.
A sparse autoencoder split an InceptionV1 neuron into generic and fur-specific boundary detectors.
Tracing circuits driving one ResNet-50 neuron showed windmills and dog ears shared one triangular-shape feature.
In nine transformers, apparent word-sense mixing in MLP neurons reflected word form, mainly in early-to-mid layers.
A forum post's informal look at GPT-2 XL found no neurons for unrelated concepts.
Sparse autoencoders split two other InceptionV1 neurons into distinct low-level features, not one shared feature.
Transcoder features grouped one Gemma 3 4B neuron's contexts into distinct concept clusters, not one feature.
Adjusting polysemanticity scores for word form reclassified only 6.5–10.4% of GPT-2 neurons flagged as polysemantic.
Even when explained by concept combinations, 31% of ResNet-18 units still fired for unrelated concepts.
Pruning an AlexNet neuron's upstream weights found separate terrier and metal-cylinder circuits, not one shared feature.
Clustering activations split three other neurons' mixed responses into distinct directions, not one shared feature.
Inspected across a broad range of inputs, early-layer n-gram neurons still fired for unrelated n-grams.
Tracing circuits driving three other ResNet-50 neurons found a separate circuit for each concept.
Randomly sampled Claude 3 Sonnet neurons were typically active in multiple unrelated contexts.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: The canonical InceptionV1 neuron 4e:55 (cat faces and car fronts) and the pose reading named in the statement. No study re-analyses 4e:55 or any Zoom In example with SAEs, attribution clustering or pruning. arXiv:2406.03662 re-analyses other InceptionV1 neurons (conv2d1/n/44, mixed3b/n/359, n/376). n/44 and n/359 are covered under against (limits_scope); n/376 is covered under wording_issues[0], not under support.
untested.basis: The original's row DOI:10.23915/distill.00024.001#R2 (cannot_determine; reads 4e:55 as having no shared feature). The untested-parts lines of arXiv:2006.14032, arXiv:2305.01610, arXiv:2404.06453, arXiv:2605.29358, arXiv:2610.24521, lw:JA5Eyf2cqyL3HbKxS, and arXiv:2604.00443 ('pose-type shared features'). counts: versions.V6.original_sources_linked lists only DOI:10.23915/distill.00024.001.

untested.what: A rate of truly unrelated mixtures among randomly sampled neurons after per-neuron re-analysis with SAEs, transcoders or attribution clustering, in InceptionV1 or in any language model. The only post-tool random-sample rate is for ResNet-18 with compositional formulas (arXiv:2006.14032#r1). Claude 3 Sonnet: the judgement that 50 randomly sampled MLP neurons typically fire in multiple unrelated contexts comes from manual inspection (arXiv:2605.29358#r1). The same study also scores 100 random neurons with automated interpretability (Claude 3 Opus) and previous-layer neurons with an automated specificity rubric. Both scores are only relative to SAE features (from the checker's reading of the text; no row). It gives no per-neuron decomposition and no rate of unrelated mixtures. The lexical adjustment in arXiv:2604.00443 covers polysemous words only.
untested.basis: The untested-parts lines of arXiv:2406.03662, arXiv:2404.06453, arXiv:2610.24521, arXiv:2605.29358, arXiv:2304.09707 and arXiv:2604.00443. counts: versions.V6.coverage_by_operation.probing.studies = 3, and none of those three studies reports a sample-wide rate.

wording_issues.issue: The only canonical neuron in the pack is InceptionV1 4e:55. It appears only in the original, which reads it as having no shared feature (DOI:10.23915/distill.00024.001#R2). The studies test random, probe-selected or hand-picked neurons instead. In the InceptionV1 SAE study, the neurons the author calls polysemantic are early-vision ones, conv2d1/n/44 and mixed3b/n/359. They give that study's only V6 verdict, limits_scope (arXiv:2406.03662#r1, #r3). The same study's boundary neuron mixed3b/n/376 is listed among 'more monosemantic corresponding neurons', so it does not test V6 (r2; the check sets its V6 verdict to none).

Within one study, the same tool can give both outcomes on different neurons. PURE finds a shared feature for ResNet-50 #271 (arXiv:2404.06453#r24) but distinct circuits for #1929 (lipstick and boar), #1381 and #915 (r4, r16, r18). Activation clustering finds related directions for Inception V3 neuron 1 (arXiv:2304.09707#r3) but distinct ones for neurons 35, 5 and 27 (r1, r8, r10). In a ResNet-18 random sample of 128 units with length-10 compositional explanations, the authors sort 28 of the 88 meaningful units as joining lexically unrelated concepts. By inspection, they read those concepts as sharing one perceptual feature (arXiv:2006.14032#r2). Yet 31% of the 128 units remain polysemantic (r1). In InceptionV1, SAEs split both neurons the author calls polysemantic, n/44 and n/359, into distinct features rather than one shared feature (arXiv:2406.03662#r1, #r3). The split of n/376 into related offshoots (r2) is on a neuron the author calls more monosemantic, so it is not a V6 case.

No row tests pose. The shared features actually found are a triangular shape (ResNet-50 #271, arXiv:2404.06453#r24), word form (arXiv:2604.00443#r01) and a perceptual feature such as vertical rails (ResNet-18, arXiv:2006.14032#r2). The ResNet-18 authors read the vertical rails from the masked images by inspection. Broden has no vertical-rails label, so the formula search itself did not name that feature. In language models the shared feature is the token's identity across senses (polysemy), which is a different kind of explanation from an abstract visual feature.

wording_issues.phrase: so truly unrelated mixtures are rare
wording_issues.issue: 31% of a random sample of 128 ResNet-18 units remain polysemantic after compositional explanation (arXiv:2006.14032#r1). Random Claude 3 Sonnet neurons are typically active in multiple unrelated contexts (arXiv:2605.29358#r1). arXiv:2604.00443 does not estimate how common unrelated mixtures are. About 57% of the activating pairs of its flagged neurons share a word form, on polysemous inputs only, with the model not named (r27). Its lexically adjusted score reclassifies 6.5–10.4% of flagged GPT-2 neurons, and 93–94% of those are confirmed form detectors (Section 5.7, no row). The authors call this a conservative lower bound, because it corrects only the top-50 form detectors per word, and they describe flagged neurons as predominantly lexical detectors. Outside polysemous-word inputs, the only support for 'rare' is an anecdote with no method (lw:JA5Eyf2cqyL3HbKxS#r1).

wording_issues.phrase: truly unrelated ... related offshoots of one job
wording_issues.issue: The statement gives no criterion for relatedness, and the studies judge it qualitatively (verdict reasons of arXiv:2305.01610 and arXiv:2304.09707). The authors of arXiv:2304.09707 call neuron 1's clusters not entirely conceptually different (r3, partial). On the same neuron, #271, CLIP and attribution clustering disagree on whether the concepts are related (arXiv:2404.06453#r24). The InceptionV1 SAE splits are a middle case that the statement does not name, and that study states no criterion for relatedness either. n/44 splits into several low-level feature types: brightness gradients, colour contrast and complex Gabor filters (arXiv:2406.03662#r1). n/359 responds to curves in two very different orientations and splits into two curve detectors plus a double-curve detector (r3). The verdict treats these features as not clearly unrelated and gives limits_scope.

method_sensitivity.factor: Clustering space (circuit attributions vs semantic embedding)
method_sensitivity.what: ResNet-50 neuron #271: CLIP-embedding clustering separates dog ears from windmills, while PURE attribution clustering shows one triangular-shape feature (arXiv:2404.06453#r24). The PURE record says that separation depends on the clustering method (PURE vs activations), the number of clusters, the architecture and the evaluation embedding.

Inception V3 Mixed 7b clusters were reported at dmax=15 (arXiv:2304.09707#r1, #r3). The record says dmax changes how fine the concepts are and can merge or split clusters, which decides whether a neuron's image groups count as one concept or several.

InceptionV1 double-curve neuron mixed3b/n/359 (base SAE L1 3.5e-6, 8x expansion). The authors trained two more SAEs at higher L1 coefficients, values not stated, to test whether the double-curve feature was an SAE failure. As L1 rises, the analogous double-curve feature's maximum activation falls and the left and right single-curve features' maxima rise (arXiv:2406.03662#r4, figure only, Figure 3 bottom). The double-curve feature weakens but does not vanish: analogous features exist at every L1 tried. So sparsity strength changes how much weight the shared double-curve feature gets relative to the single-curve features, but not whether it appears.

method_sensitivity.factor: Part of the activation distribution examined, and summary metric
method_sensitivity.what: Gemma 3 4B L22: the record says peak-only contexts give neuron sort-eval scores comparable to transcoder features, while quantile sampling gives noticeably worse neuron scores. The N5039+ clusters use only the top 4096 activations (arXiv:2610.24521#R3). In arXiv:2305.01610, F1 and raw activation counts give different pictures for the is_title neuron (r9). Its record also says athlete-type neurons read as general sport neurons from per-token averages rather than max-activating examples (not in rows).

GPT-2 (117M), cosine lexical contribution ratio Rlex: .735 at layer 0 (arXiv:2604.00443#r02), .399 at layer 10 (r12) and .290 at layer 11, GPT-2's minimum (r13). LLaMA-2-70B (NF4, 80 layers) has a layer-averaged Rlex of 0.45 (r14). The check of the text adds the following, which no row records. BERT and ELECTRA decline more steeply than GPT-2. ELECTRA reaches its minimum of .250 at layer 6, then rises to .542 at layer 11. LLaMA-2-13B reaches 0.25 at layer 38. LLaMA-2-70B stays at about 0.35-0.45 across its 80 layers. The Rlex CI stays above zero in all models. How much word form explains neuron co-activation therefore depends on the layer, and the depth trajectory depends on the model family. The fall with depth is not uniform.

method_sensitivity.factor: Pruning target (semantic category vs random split)
method_sensitivity.what: Regularized AlexNet Conv5:9: subcircuits pruned for category-specific targets (terrier vs metal cylinder) diverge (arXiv:2206.01627#R3, #R5). Random halves of the same mixed patch set give overlapping subcircuits (R6, control).

In arXiv:2006.14032, longer formulas improve explanation fit (record's method-sensitivity line). The study does not report whether this changes the share of units sorted as polysemantic; the 31% and the 88-unit breakdown are at maximum length 10 (r1, r2).

status_amendment.public_note: The status now limits the contested rating to the claim that truly unrelated mixtures are rare, and marks the Claude 3 Sonnet and Pythia sparse-probing studies as work by the original authors' group rather than independent tests. The level is unchanged and still rests mainly on one independent random sample of image-classifier neurons.
